summary: Holt Hill tower in Andover, MA: a 1924 tower replaced by a 68-foot steel tower in 1970; in active use but not open to the public. Staffing history and fires not found.

facts.agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control (Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation)

access.note: In active use but not open to the public, per the Ward Reservation article on Wikipedia

events.note: Fire tower built at the top of Holt Hill; one of four Essex County towers built that year
Current 68-foot steel tower with 10-by-10-foot wooden cab
Registered December 15, 2004 as US 606, MA 17; nominated by Henry Isenberg

evidence.supports: third of four Essex County towers built in 1924; Andover tower replaced in 1970
evidence.quote: The third of four towers built in Essex County in 1924, Andover Fire Tower was replaced in 1970.

evidence.quote: It is in active use, but is not open to the public.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's Built field and Wikipedia both date the current tower to 1970. Wikipedia also dates the earlier tower on Holt Hill to 1924, so both are recorded: the brief's 1970 build date is kept and the 1924 tower is added as an event.

sources.title: Forest Fire Control Suppression and Detection Programs

notes_for_editor: The 1924 tower and the current access status rest on Wikipedia's Ward Reservation article, which cites a 2017 Andover Townsman piece by Gail Ralston, 'Holt Hill Part 2: The fire tower'. That article returned HTTP 429 to both fetch_text and WebFetch, so it could not be read; retry later, as it is the likeliest source for staffing history and notable fires. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Massachusetts Facebook post calling 1970 'the year it was built' could not be read and is not used. The Mass.gov page is undated and does not name Andover. No photos recorded.
